title: Book One · Chapter 111: Two Empty Crates
story:
“Let me see the empty crates first,” Mrs Lan says. “Then I can decide.”

Mr Qiu comes after breakfast. The rain is only a fine mist now. He does not bring his stock yet. Mr Han carries one empty wooden crate. Dad carries another on his way to work.

The crates are wider than Ronan expected. Together they take up the whole dry mat by the door.

“Not there,” Mrs Lan says. “I need to get past.”

Dad carries them into the front room. He sets them along the side wall. Mrs Lan measures the walking space with her own feet. She opens the cupboard door. There must be room for it to move.

“These can stay here for now,” she says. “We will talk about the next step later. Only dry things can stay. You cannot sell things from my room. Customers cannot come in to look.”

Mr Qiu agrees. They speak about a first check in three days. But Mr Qiu still has no new place for his stall.

Ronan has his CLOSED TODAY card ready. He stays out of the adults' way. He holds his card up.

Mr Qiu reads it. “Clear letters. May I use it?”

Ronan nods. “I made it for you.”

“Thank you. We need string to tie it up. We must put it somewhere dry enough to read.”

Dad gives him a short piece of string. Mr Qiu puts the card in his bag. The children will not climb or tie anything to the roof.

Leo arrives at the gate with his mother. She is dropping off a pair of trousers for Mum. He sees the crates. “Are these ships?” he asks.

“Book ships,” Ronan says.

“Dry book ships,” Mrs Lan adds. “They must stay on this side of my room.”

She gives the boys two pieces of paper to label the lids. Mr Qiu asks for simple numbers: one and two. He will list the things in each crate.

Leo wants to draw pencils on both. Ronan remembers the shared school page and asks Mr Qiu first.

“Numbers are enough today,” Mr Qiu says. “We may put different things inside later.”

They make the numbers large. Dad checks the labels beside the handholds. The handholds must stay clear. Then he leaves for Mr Sun's. He needs to reach work on time. He still needs to work those hours.

Mr Han takes one empty crate back to the stall. Mr Qiu takes the other. They will pack the dry goods first. Then they will get help to carry the crates. The six damp exercise books stay apart on their tray.

Ronan feels disappointed when the front room is empty again. The adults talked for much of the morning. So far, he can see only two paper numbers. But they agreed on a place for the crates.

Mrs Lan folds the dry mat out of the way.

“Now people can walk.”

“Will we carry the boxes in heavy rain?” he asks.

“The adults will check the weather first. Then they will choose a safe time for the boxes. We do not need to rush.”

Mum calls the boys to get their shoes. They are in the way by the kitchen door. Leo picks up his own. Ronan picks up his, then returns for a loose lace.

The room is ready for the crates. For the moment, it is still clear for Mrs Lan. She lives here and must use her own room. Ronan looks at the clear way to her chair. The crates must not block that space.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- handholds＝提手孔
- mist＝薄雾
- agreed＝商定了
- for the moment＝眼下

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：mat＝门垫；label＝标签；lace＝鞋带。

## 读句提示

**Then I can decide.**

然后／我／才能决定。先看空箱，再决定是否借地方。

## 理解问题

1. MrsLan借出前屋时明确了哪些界限？
2. 为什么木箱暂时又被搬走？
